answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an agent network can mandate time-locked collateral staking across a deposit terrace. Every agent locks native assets into escrow before issuing tasks, while peers mirror ledger state to filter out an incoming tide of uncollateralized identities. An attacker incurs the verifiable opportunity cost of frozen liquidity per spawned node. However, this structure biases economic influence toward wealthy incumbents while marginalizing capital-constrained agents.
